title: sandboxPrefixForLaunch forces allow_network true for every dispatch; a profile's allow_network false is a WARN, not a boundary
problem: launch.go threads sandbox.allow_network from the profile into the Config, but sandboxPrefixForLaunch overrides it to true for every dispatch that reaches the wrapper and only prints a WARN; TestSandboxPrefix_ForcesNetwork pins that. So no profile can confine a phase's network today: a helper with read access to most of the tree (deny_read_subpaths is docs/private only) can send what it reads anywhere. Found by the ADR-0106 security re-review of the recovery agent's profile (2026-09-26), which declares allow_network false as intent. The filesystem grant (read_only_repo, deny_subpaths) is the only OS boundary that holds.
fix: Honour allow_network false in the wrapper for profiles that declare it (the SBPL and bwrap generators already model the network rule), keep the forced-true path only for the CLIs whose REPL cannot boot offline and say which those are in the manifest, and turn the WARN into a refusal when a profile declares false and the driver cannot comply. Update the pin test to the new contract and make sandbox_deliverable_recovery_test.go exercise the real launch path.
acceptance: A profile with sandbox.allow_network false launches with the network denied on the darwin and linux wrappers, or is refused with a coded signal naming the driver.
A profile that leaves allow_network unset keeps today's behaviour.
The recovery agent's profile test goes through sandboxPrefixForLaunch, not a hand-built request.
